Data concerning the occurrence of flood peaks and volumes is also very limited in the Project Area. Numerous studies involving areal analysis of peak flows have been conducted at various times during the last few years. These studies attempt to describe potential peak flows at selected unmeasured sites. The study technique involves using regression equations which describe peak discharges for various recurrence intervals in terms of certain basin and channel characteristics. Using these equations, peak discharges can be estimated at ungaged sites. For example, the peak flow having a probability of recurrance of 10 years in the Sarpy Creek area is estimated to be about 22 cubic feet per second per square mile on drainages 2 to 5 square miles in size. A graph showing the estimated peak discharges for various recurrence intervals on major streams in the project area is shown in Figure II-4. Surface Water Use - Surface waters in the Project Area are utilized for watering livestock, irrigation of small gardens, and to a limited extent, domestic purposes. In the Sarpy Creek basin there exist 53 water rights appropriations, totaling 740 cubic feet per second. In the leased area there are 13 appropriations totaling 193 cubic feet per second.
